# Invocations TestAgentSurfaces should not resolve against the cobra tree —
# normally a command documented before it ships. One normalized invocation per
# line, exactly as written in the markdown. Every entry needs a comment saying
# why it is here and what removes it.

# Draft spec 026 5.4's decomposition stamp. lode:splitting-specs-into-plans
# names the command while telling authors it does not exist yet and to keep
# writing fullCoverageWith. Remove both entries when 026 5.4 ships and the
# skill stops hedging.
lode decompose <ref>
lode decompose

# Spec 061 §1's naming law (internal/cmd/CLAUDE.md "Naming") states the
# pattern itself. `<entity>` and `<verb>` are placeholders, so this can never
# resolve however real the surface gets. Remove it only if the law's wording
# stops spelling the pattern as an invocation, or the test learns to skip a
# command whose first token is a placeholder.
lode <entity> <verb>

# Also from 061 §1: commands the naming law names before they ship. The
# rename lands across WL-471..WL-477 and `work` arrives with its own part;
# `next` and `status` are two of the L9 shortcuts, which can only be
# registered once `work next` and `work status` exist. Remove each once its
# command does.
lode work
lode next
lode status

# internal/cmd/CLAUDE.md "Checking whether a command still resolves" documents
# how to detect a command that is gone, so its examples have to name one. The
# placeholder form cannot resolve for the same reason `lode <entity> <verb>`
# cannot. Remove these only if that section stops using a worked example.
lode <path> --help
lode task ready 2>&1 | head -1     # unknown command "ready" for "lode task"
